description: The five assist tiers and the adaptive router that recommends one. Tier parameters were previously only a table in the design bible; they belong here because every number is a balance lever tuned in beta. See docs/design-bible.md section 2.1 and the D4 entry in docs/open-decisions.md.

tiers.name: Show
tiers.notes: Never auto-routed. Show is a deliberate accessibility choice a player makes for themselves; routing someone here on the strength of one tutorial reads as a verdict rather than a suggestion.

tiers.name: Senior
tiers.notes: The intended experience. The game is balanced and marketed around this tier.

tiers.name: Patch
tiers.notes: Never auto-routed. Patch tier is chosen, not assigned.

router.source_note: The Patch already scores the player's figure-eight tracing against a reference curve by distance transform. That number was previously discarded after grading; the router is the only new thing here, and it is roughly two weeks of design work.
router.sample: best 3 of the final 5 attempts, to reward the learning curve rather than the first fumble
router.fallback_note: Applied when The Patch is skipped entirely, or when fewer than 5 attempts were made.

presentation.explanation_source: the player's own tracing, overlaid on the reference
presentation.example_copy: Your edges held clean but the lobes drifted wide. Novice looks like the right place to start — you can change this whenever you like.
presentation.override_cost: one input, always available, never buried in a submenu

reoffer.note: The router is allowed to be wrong exactly once, and to say so. Offered only after the trigger, never applied automatically.

beta_metric.name: router accuracy
beta_metric.definition: 1 − (share of players who override the recommended tier within their first hour)
beta_metric.note: New wave 1 question in the beta plan. A router that is overridden by half its players is worse than a fixed default, because it has spent the player's trust to arrive at the same place.
